lesson.title: Amble & Go
lesson.subtitle: The ambulāre etymology; vais, vas, va, allons, allez in motion drills.

hook.title: Why aller Has Two Ancient Families Inside One Verb
hook.content: Singular je vais (/vɛ/), tu vas (/va/), il/elle/on va (/va/) come from Latin vādere ('to advance'), while aller, nous allons (/alɔ̃/), and vous allez (/ale/) come from Latin ambulāre ('to walk/amble', root of English amble and ambulance)!

footnotes.title: Why 'ambulance' is a cousin of aller
footnotes.content: A field hospital that walked along with the French army was called a 'walking hospital' (hôpital ambulant, from ambulāre)!

pattern.title: Going Somewhere: aller + au / à la / à l' / chez
pattern.content: Use vais, vas, va, allons, allez with destinations.
pattern.linguist_note: Suppletion in Romance 'go' (vādere + ambulāre) is shared across French and Italian.
pattern.trap_note: Don't say *je va or *tu vais: je takes vais (-ai-), while tu vas and il/on va both sound like /va/!

exercises.prompt: Match each subject with its present-tense form of aller:
exercises.meaning: je (I go), tu (you go, informal), il / elle / on (goes / we go), nous (we go — ambulāre), vous (you go — ambulāre)
exercises.explanation: Singular uses the v- stem; plural uses the regular all- stem.

exercises.prompt: The all- stem of French aller / allons (from Latin ambulāre 'to walk') hides inside which English word for a leisurely walk?
exercises.explanation: Latin ambulāre gave English amble/ambulance and French aller.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask a friend 'Where are you going?'
Answer the question in the negative using ne ... pas:
exercises.reply_idea: Reply that you do not speak German.
cues: Begin with Je ne parle pas...
exercises.explanation: French wraps ne and pas tightly around the conjugated verb parle.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Je vais au cinéma avec mon ami
exercises.target_answer: Je vais au cinéma avec mon ami
exercises.meaning: I am going to the cinema with my friend
exercises.explanation: à + le cinéma fuses into au cinéma.
exercises.affirmation: You wrote Je vais au cinéma avec mon ami cleanly.

summary.outcome: Conjugate aller across all persons (vais, vas, va, allons, allez) and pair it with destinations.

use_example.german: Où est-ce que vous allez ? — Nous allons à la gare.
use_example.english: Where are you going? — We are going to the station.

summary.takeaway: je vais (/vɛ/), tu vas (/va/), il/on va (/va/), nous allons, vous allez.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([1202] Future Gym): see how Amble & Go leads directly into Future Gym.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "I am going to the cinema with my friend" in French:
twist.target_answer: Je vais au cinéma avec mon ami
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Je vais au cinéma avec mon ami" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Amble & Go.

aller.context_translation: I'm going to go to the café.
aller.etymology_derivation: Latin ambulāre 'to walk' → ambler → aller. To go is a stroll away — and the near future rides on it.

je_vais.etymology_derivation: vais is aller's only irregular card in je; with an infinitive after it, it makes the future.

allons.etymology_derivation: Regular stem all- returns in nous allons and vous allez.

allez.etymology_derivation: Also shouted at sports matches: 'Allez !' ('Come on!').

on.context_translation: Shall we go to the café?
on.etymology_derivation: on is worn-down homme — 'the man says' became 'one says' became spoken French's everyday 'we'. The nasal vowel is the fossil.

où.etymology_derivation: Latin ubi 'where' — the root English borrowed wholesale in 'ubiquitous' (present everywhere).

gare.etymology_derivation: Originally a river shelter where boats pulled in.

train.context_phrase: Le train part à huit heures.
train.etymology_derivation: Old French traïn 'a line of things pulled along'.
